chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer

Regarding the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Save yourselves and your families from a Fire.' I said, 'How can one save them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Enjoin with what Allah has Commanded with, and forbid them from what Allah has Forbidden them. So if they obey you, you would have saved them, and if they disobey you, you would have fulfilled what is upon you.'

key_terms.قَضَيْتَ مَا عَلَيْكَ: You have fulfilled what is upon you (duty)

ai.seo_question: How does one practically save their family from Hellfire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the obligation of 'saving' one's family is fulfilled through the active practice of *amr bil-ma'ruf wa nahy anil-munkar* (enjoining good and forbidding evil). It establishes a legal principle where the head of the household is exempt from further accountability if they diligently instruct their family, regardless of whether the family ultimately obeys or disobeys, highlighting the distinction between duty and outcome in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer,

‘Regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [66:6] O you who believe! Save yourselves and your families from a Fire. I said, ‘How can one save them?’ Heasws said: ‘Enjoin with what Allahazwj has Commanded with, and forbid them from what Allahazwj has Forbidden them. So if they obey you, you would have save them, and if they disobey you, you would have fulfilled what is upon you’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Uthaman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah from abu Basir from who has said the following:

“About the words of Allah, the most Majestic, the most Glorious, ‘. . . Save yourselves and your family from a fire. . . .’ [66:6] I asked him (the Imam), ‘How can I save them?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘You must order them to do what Allah has commanded to do and prohibit them from what Allah has prohibited them to do. If they obeyed you, you have saved them. If they disobeyed you, you have fulfilled your responsibility.’”
